CONFIRMED

- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-host-sqlite\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\sqlite\SqliteHostStorePersistence.java:38-108` opens the database and only executes `CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS`. Lines 77-83 create `ji_host_timeline`, but there is no schema-version check, migration, scan of `ji_host_sessions`, or projection backfill.
- `SqliteHostStorePersistence.java:228-262` reads history exclusively from `ji_host_timeline`. Lines 231-235 only confirm that the canonical session exists; if no timeline rows exist, lines 237-259 return an empty page without decoding or backfilling `ji_host_sessions.document`.
- The sole population path is `save()` at lines 212-225, which invokes `replaceTimelineProjection()`. Its insert logic is at lines 437-462. Reopening or reading a legacy database never invokes this path, so history remains empty until some later save happens.
- `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-host-sqlite\src\test\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\sqlite\SqliteHostStorePersistenceTest.java:118-155` only tests databases whose timeline rows were populated through the new `save()` implementation before reopening. It does not test a populated legacy `ji_host_sessions` table with no timeline table or rows.
